items.text: The review of the Children's Rights Association's performance in 1404 shows that child sexual abuse is the top issue in the cases referred to the association. These cases include sexual violence and abuse by family members and others, as well as threats and assaults in cyberspace. Despite extensive supervision over sexual matters, the Iranian government has not established a strong support system to protect children from sexual violence.

Farid Ramazani was killed in Tehran on the evening of January 8 by forces of the Islamic Republic. His uncle, who lives in Denmark, said the forces shot Farid and then gave him a coup de grâce. They also targeted the finger with a crown tattoo.

Mehdi Chamran, head of Tehran City Council, said participants of the Janfodayan rally came from various ages and professions to show support for the leadership and the Islamic Republic. He added that the enemy is in decline and will face harsher blows if it continues on its path.

Kylian Mbappé ended his nearly 20-year partnership with Nike and joined the Swiss brand On, becoming the main face of the company's entry into the football shoe market. He also received part of the company's shares. Thierry Henry, as On's football director, played a role in convincing Mbappé to join.

Ahmad Alamolhoda stated in Friday prayers in Mashhad that women without hijab should not be allowed to enter universities as it may lead to gatherings of agitators. He described the university as a sanctuary and called for decisive action by security and judicial authorities. Alamolhoda emphasized that if administrative bodies fail to control the issue, security forces must intervene.

Hossein Ghashghaei, Sara Shamsaei, and Abolfazl Ghashghaei were arrested by security forces nine days ago. Their place of detention and status remain unknown. Hossein and Sara were arrested in Lahijan, and Abolfazl in Zarandieh.

In the first week of the Iranian Women's Premier Football League, Persepolis defeated Tehran 2-0. Esteghlal and Sepahan also won with the same score. Gol Gohar Sirjan beat Varash Nowshahr 4-1 and became the league leader.

The fourth anniversary of the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement is being held tonight at the main Paris city hall. The event is attended by Iranians living in France, human rights defenders, political activists, and cultural figures. The report and interview were conducted by an Iran International journalist.

Turkey will stop flights of Mahan Air to and from the country starting September 21. This decision follows the sanctioning of three Turkish companies for providing services to Mahan. Turkish officials stated that the ban does not include all Iranian airlines but the risk of cooperation with other companies is being reviewed.

People have reported feeling more comfort and freedom after the removal of mandatory hijab, and the city has become more beautiful. They also mentioned reduced expenses and a change in men's attitudes toward women. This change has made individuals feel more empowered and confident.

Donald Trump stated that the Islamic Republic of Iran wants an agreement with the United States but will not consider it if it is not a good deal. He also said his administration is talking with the Houthis to explore the possibility of a deal. Trump added that Iran is failing financially and militarily, which is why it wants an agreement.

Two separate attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have been reported. The Islamic Republic stated that one of the ships was passing illegally. Donald Trump also announced that a major decision regarding military operations against the Islamic Republic is approaching.

Mark Carney, the Prime Minister of Canada, is making a historic visit to the Saint Pierre and Miquelon archipelago to meet with Emmanuel Macron. They will discuss cooperation in energy, critical minerals, advanced technologies, and defense coordination. Addressing the impacts of climate change is also part of their talks.

Sara Regensburger, an Iranian-German fashion designer, presented her Spring/Summer 2027 collection titled "Diaspora: The Art of Belonging" at London Fashion Week. The collection is inspired by growing up between two cultures and blends Western tailoring with Iranian details. She also aims to showcase Iranian culture beyond the news.

The US Central Command announced that by September 17, it had redirected 105 commercial ships as part of the US blockade against Iran. CENTCOM released a video showing the USS Boxer operations in the Arabian Sea. The ship and its deployed Marines continue to enforce the blockade.

The mother of Mahna Doukoshkani lit a candle at her daughter's grave as part of the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign. Mahna Doukoshkani, 18 years old, was shot and killed by officers in Kermanshah on January 8, 2026.

Workers in the service section of Bandar Imam Khomeini Municipality reported non-payment of two months' wages and delays in insurance payments. Workers in the security and executive sections also face wage arrears.

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, described the rescue operation of two American pilots in Iran. One pilot was injured and trapped in a mountainous area. The operation demonstrated the US military's commitment to recovering its personnel.

Yashar Soltani, an Iranian journalist, said in a video interview that Iran's oil sales have been entrusted to four people. He said these four people earned $1.5 billion from discounts on the sale of 80 million barrels of oil alone, apart from their other income from these sales.

The Housing Foundation offices have received funds for war damage compensation but have not paid them. The price of the cancer drug Tedrox has increased from 19 million to 95 million, making it unaffordable for people. Additionally, issues such as delays in car delivery, contaminated tap water in Khalkhal, and unpaid wages at the Marine Engineering and Construction Company have been reported.

Mohammad Radman-Nia, a 29-year-old bodybuilder, was shot on the evening of Friday, January 9, 2026, in the Nezamabad neighborhood of Tehran. He died a day later due to the severity of his injuries. His mother vowed in a video at his grave to continue his path.

Given the developments in Yemen and the insistence of the Islamic Republic on sabotage in Hormuz, the US is preparing for the scenario of restarting attacks. This indicates rising tensions in the region. Further details are not provided in the text.

The spokesperson for the US Treasury Department told Al Jazeera that the department has initiated strict measures against banks supporting Mahan Air in the UAE and Turkey. He added that Turkey and Oman have also suspended Mahan flights. The spokesperson for the US Treasury Department stated on Friday, September 17, that these measures have had "tangible results," including the suspension of Mahan flights in Turkey and Oman.

A memorial birthday ceremony for Alireza Rabat Jozi was held at his gravesite. Alireza Rabat Jozi, 35 years old, was killed by a direct gunshot on January 9, 2026, in Nazarabad, Karaj. The video of the ceremony was recently released.

Hasan Şaş, former Turkish national football player, and Yağız Sabuncuoğlu, journalist and sports commentator, were arrested in Bakırköy prosecutor's investigation on facilitating drug use. Arrest warrants were issued for 18 people including actors, singers, and social media figures. New investigations have started as part of efforts to combat drug use.

Seyed Ahmad Seyed Abdollahi, a political prisoner, returned to Borujen prison after his leave ended. He returned to prison on Monday, 9 Shahrivar, and his leave had started on 3 Shahrivar. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

In a secret meeting in Germany, the United States is preparing to return to operations. This topic was discussed in the audio version of Harf Akhar with Pouria Zeraati. More details were reviewed in this meeting.

The Washington Post, citing six US officials, reported that at least 22 US troops have been killed in the Iran war, four more than the public Pentagon tally. One official said not all unrecorded cases are directly war-related, but these troops were present in Middle East conflicts. The US Department of Defense did not respond to the Post's question about the discrepancy.

A citizen reported to Iran International that the newly supplied gasoline burns inside the car more than twice as fast as before. He expressed concern about what has been added to the gasoline. The reason for this change is unknown.

People from across Iran have reported economic difficulties and high medical expenses. Cancer patients and those needing surgery complain about high costs and insurance issues. Additionally, blind students and unemployed individuals mention financial pressures due to inflation and lack of support.

For the first time, men officially watched a match of the Iranian women's Premier League football in person. The match between Esteghlal and Palayesh Gaz Ilam was held at Kargar Stadium in Tehran with male spectators present. Maryam Irandoost became emotional after the game when talking about her father's presence, and Nosrat Irandoost expressed satisfaction with his daughter's performance.

Houshang Hasan-Yari stated that the European naval coalition cannot replace direct US support without practical action and military presence. He added that the Islamic Republic is unlikely to control the Houthis as it considers them a strategic leverage. Addressing Houthi attacks requires a more serious approach toward the Islamic Republic.

A meeting titled "From War to the Negotiation Table" is being held in the US Congress on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. The event aims to draw American policymakers' attention to the consequences of war and negotiations for the Iranian people. The organizer, Siamak Aram, emphasized the role and demands of citizens who bear the greatest cost of these developments.

The Iran under-23 football team will play its second match against China in the Asian Games in Nagoya on Sunday morning Tehran time. This match is part of the Asian Games competition. The report is by Alireza Modiri, Iran International correspondent in Japan.

Matin Tahmasbi, a firefighter, wore a commemorative T-shirt of Hamid Mahdavi during the 10-kilometer race in Tehran. Hamid Mahdavi was a firefighter and athlete from Mashhad who was killed on January 8, 2026, while helping protesters. The scene of his aid to a protester received widespread attention.

Trump stated that the Islamic Republic will never have nuclear weapons and the war will end soon. He said Americans are paying extra costs to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. He also predicted that gasoline prices will return to pre-war levels once the current situation ends.

Saudi Civil Defense issued a danger warning in several cities including Jeddah, Taif, Yanbu, Khamis Mushait, Jazan, and Al-Ula. Later, it announced that the danger was lifted in Jeddah, Taif, Yanbu, Abha, Khamis Mushait, and Jazan. This announcement was made on Friday.

Ghasan Ashour, Middle East analyst, said the increase in European and Arab naval presence aims to prevent Houthi domination of the Bab el-Mandeb and Iran's domination of the Strait of Hormuz. He added that Saudi Arabia seeks sustainable deterrence in the Red Sea, but without US support, achieving this goal will face serious challenges.

Alireza Nourizadeh stated that the sale of F-35 fighters to Saudi Arabia is mainly to strengthen deterrence against the Islamic Republic rather than to confront the Houthis. He also emphasized that Europe cannot remain indifferent to the security of Bab al-Mandab. Disruptions in shipping through this route affect Europe's energy security.

Four years have passed since the killing of Mahsa Zhina Amini, a 22-year-old woman, in the custody of the Islamic Republic's morality police. This incident sparked an unprecedented uprising in Iran, with the sports community also participating in the protests. The program Hattrick has covered this topic.

Molavi Abdolhamid referred to the anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death and the killing of protesters, stating that if officials had paid attention to people's demands, these events would not have happened. He mentioned the protests of 2019, 2022, and December 2025, describing them as bitter and tragic. He also criticized the entry of foreign and proxy forces into Sistan and Baluchestan province.

Esteghlal and Tractor football teams faced Al Sadd Qatar and Shabab Al Ahli UAE in the first week of the Elite League. Mozdek Mirzayi discussed this in the Hat-trick program. The full version of the Hat-trick program is available to watch.

Pakistani officials have called for the resumption of negotiations between the Islamic Republic and the United States based on the Islamabad agreement. They have also requested an immediate halt to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Pakistan has asked Iran to use its influence to convince the Houthis to stop attacks, especially on Saudi energy facilities.

Farzin Nadimi, a senior researcher in defense and security affairs, stated that the increase in American military casualties will affect the intensity and method of Washington's military operations more than it changes the principle of continuing the war. He added that the experience of recent attacks will push the US towards reducing reliance on fixed bases and moving towards the deployment of more dispersed, mobile, and standoff forces and systems.

The US State Department announced that the purchase of 48 F-35 fighter jets will significantly enhance Saudi Arabia's air power and deterrence. Washington emphasized that this deal will strengthen Saudi Arabia's military cooperation with the US and other regional partners. More details are provided by Kambiz Tavana on Iran International.

Trump signed the congressional bill sanctioning Iran and Russia. The bill includes sanctions on Iran's energy and arms sectors and expands the president's authority to impose tariffs on energy customers of Tehran and Moscow. The new law also imposes sanctions on Vladimir Putin and Russian officials.

The Trump administration has imposed new restrictions on the Iranian delegation attending the UN General Assembly in New York. The delegation is only allowed to move within a limited area between the airport, hotel, and UN headquarters and cannot shop at certain stores. The UN General Assembly begins in two days, and this delegation is the only one facing such restrictions.

Choo Hyun, South Korea's foreign minister, emphasized his country's readiness to participate practically in restoring free passage through the Strait of Hormuz during a meeting with his American counterpart. South Korea is considering possible participation in efforts to restore safe shipping but has not yet decided to deploy military forces. The South Korean president stated that the country will not send military forces to wars outside its borders.

Trump announced that the US has reached an agreement with Denmark and Greenland giving the US permanent control over Greenland's security. The agreement will cost the US nothing, and a broad military presence in Greenland will begin. Denmark's Prime Minister's office also announced an upcoming agreement to strengthen security in the Arctic region.

Saudi Civil Defense declared normal status after issuing a warning about a potential danger in Riyadh and Al-Kharj. A Reuters reporter reported hearing two explosions in the Al-Olaya area of Riyadh. Saudi officials did not explain the source of the explosions.

Donald Trump stated that preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons is something he takes pride in. He mentioned that people might have to pay higher fuel costs temporarily to achieve this goal. Trump also predicted that the war with Iran will end soon and gasoline prices will decrease.

A senior American official stated that with the development of infrastructure and alternative oil transit routes, the Iranian government's leverage over the Strait of Hormuz is decreasing week by week. Citing statistics from the US Energy Secretary, the official said that an average of 10 to 11 million barrels of oil are being transferred daily. He added that these measures, along with the blockade and the so-called economic wrath operation, have driven the value of the rial to its lowest and inflation to its highest historical levels.

Teraneh Rahimi's cousin stated that she has difficulty walking and despite the urgent need for an MRI, she has been prevented from being transferred to the hospital. Her family bought medical equipment and medicine, but prison officials did not allow her to receive them. Additionally, the prison authorities have withheld food from Teraneh.

The Turkish banking regulator revoked the operating license of Bank Mellat's main branch in Istanbul. This decision coincided with increased US sanctions pressure on Tehran. The official Turkish notice did not cite US sanctions as the reason for the action.

Kayhan newspaper criticized some government officials' statements about hijab and described the state of nudity in Tehran's streets as concerning. The newspaper criticized the government's lack of cultural actions to improve the hijab situation in the past two years. Kayhan called for more government efforts to improve the hijab situation.

Kambiz Tavana quoted Donald Trump saying that the Islamic Republic will never acquire nuclear weapons and the war will end soon. Trump considers this a victory and describes the increase in gasoline prices as a cost for this goal. He also noted that in the coming days, the path toward an agreement or increased pressure may become clear.

Erfan Ghaneifard said that the increase in human and military costs does not change the strategic calculations of the US. He added that some statistics on casualties and war costs will not be fully disclosed until the end of the war. Greater transparency about these costs will be possible after the war ends.

The judiciary of the Islamic Republic announced the execution of Hossein Pedaran, a political prisoner linked to the 12-day war in Isfahan. He was accused of attempting to transfer sensitive military information to the Mossad. This news was announced by the judiciary.

CNN, quoting a US official, reported that Washington believes it has provided Saudi Arabia with all the necessary intelligence support and targeting data for its success against the Houthis. However, neither the US nor Saudi Arabia has a clear plan to push back the Iran-backed Houthis. A regional source also told CNN that Houthi attacks and conditions near Bab al-Mandab have affected the agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Pegah Bani Hashemi states that political executions in the past 47 years have not had a significant deterrent effect on protests. People have repeatedly stood against what they perceive as injustice. She also mentioned the impact of regional crises and political interests on Iran's human rights issues.

Ziba Aflatoun, captain of the Iranian women's national basketball team at the 1974 Asian Games, stated in an interview that one of her main reasons for emigrating was the mandatory hijab. Women's basketball in Iran first participated in the 1974 Asian Games in Tehran. The Iranian team competed with a mix of young players led by Aflatoun.

Mehdi Saremi-Far reported an AI error in a US military report that presented incorrect information. This error could have led to conflict and increased tensions, but human verification prevented it. He emphasized that there is still no comprehensive solution to prevent such errors and human review is essential.

A marathon event was held in Velayat Park, Tehran, with permission from the provincial security council, and participants pledged to observe Islamic norms. The Director General of Sports and Youth of Tehran Province stated that legal action will be taken against athletes who violate the rules. About 95% of participants complied with the regulations, and necessary warnings were issued.

Ali Dadpay stated that the cancellation of Bank Mellat's license in Istanbul has reduced banking channels between Iran and Turkey. This has pushed trade towards barter and unofficial channels. Additionally, currency inflow to the domestic market has decreased, and the Islamic Republic is facing an economic siege.
Mohammad Mohammadi Zadeh from Divandareh was arrested on Sunday, September 12, by the Intelligence Force of the IRGC. He was transferred to an unknown location. No further details have been provided.

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of War, denied the Washington Post report about higher American military casualties in the war with the Islamic Republic. He called the report fake and a complete lie. Hegseth said the newspaper's performance was even worse than the Islamic Republic's state media.
The prosecutor of Shahroud announced the arrest of 15 people related to modeling activities. Indictments have been issued for five of the detainees. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Ali Zeinivand, the spokesperson of the Ministry of Interior, stated that accusing official country leaders of compromise is a great betrayal. He also emphasized that labeling warriors and military forces as warmongers is a betrayal. He added that the majority of people desire dignified defense and resistance against the enemy.

The Judiciary Media Center announced the execution of Hossein Pedaran. He was accused of espionage and intelligence cooperation for Israel. The sentence was carried out after confirmation by the Supreme Court.

Ali Zeinivand, the spokesperson of the Ministry of Interior, stated in a press conference that criticizing the loudspeakers at nighttime gatherings is not appropriate. He added that those who gather in the squares sacrifice their comfort and are defending the people. These individuals give up their rest at night to maintain security.
Mehran Ebrahimzadeh, a resident of Mahabad, has been detained by the intelligence agency officers in the city for five days. His place of detention remains unknown.

Amir Hamidi stated that the US is simultaneously increasing the cost of confrontation and keeping negotiation channels open with the Islamic Republic. He said Trump's statements do not indicate a definite decision to end the war. The future confrontation depends on the Strait of Hormuz situation, regional attacks, and the possibility of returning to negotiations.
A video shows a large column of smoke rising in an area in northern Tehran on Saturday, 28 Shahrivar. The video was received by Iran International. No further details have been provided.

Black smoke was seen over northern Tehran due to a large fire in a 400-square-meter warehouse on Dolat Street. The warehouse contained large amounts of oil, food, and gas cylinders. No injuries or deaths have been reported so far.

A citizen reported hearing an explosion sound in Tehran on Saturday and sent a video. The transmitter's sound was reconstructed using artificial intelligence. This report was published by Iran International.
Iranians living in New Zealand held a march in Auckland on Saturday, 28 Shahrivar, to commemorate Mahsa Amini's anniversary. This event was reported through videos received by Iran International.

On 28 Shahrivar, sounds of air defense and a strong explosion were heard. Reports include economic difficulties, government forces' confrontations with citizens, and poor internet conditions. Additionally, the naval base at Hasanrud had active air defense, but the reason is unknown.

The Tehran prosecutor's office has filed charges against the organizers of the 10-kilometer marathon for not observing legal and religious regulations. The race took place on September 17, 2026, and the presence of women without mandatory hijab was notable. Officials stated that participants had signed a commitment to observe Islamic modesty.

Inter club announced that Sandro Mazzola, former captain and legend of the team, passed away at the age of 83. Mazzola spent his entire professional career at Inter, winning Serie A four times and the European championship twice. He also won the European Championship with the Italian national team and participated in several World Cups.

The Yemeni army announced that it repelled Houthi attacks in Marib province. It also recaptured positions in the western part of Taiz province. Government forces are fighting to control the heights east of Bab al-Mandab strait.

Parviz Sarvari said the Islamic Republic may have pursued nuclear weapons for deterrence. He believes Iran's participation in the NPT has brought no benefits so far. The decision to leave the NPT depends on the authorities.

Farzaneh Barzehkar, mother of Erfan Rezaei, who was killed in the "Women, Life, Freedom" uprising in Amol, shared a video about the last morning she saw her son alive. She recalled Erfan's father's memories from the Iran-Iraq war and mentioned her son's injury. The mother questioned whether her son was really dead.

Sky News Arabia reported that IRGC experts visited the port and airport of Al-Mokha and the Bab al-Mandab area. Iranian equipment has arrived in Houthi-controlled areas on Yemen's western coast. The Houthis have started installing radar on hills overlooking the Red Sea.

Hossein Abdollahi, the temporary Friday prayer leader of Dezful, said that a girl who stays late at cafes and shops will neither be a good child, a suitable mother, nor a successful spouse. He added that such a person only experiences momentary pleasures and is not inclined to planning or hard work.

The Israeli army announced that it has put its forces on full alert on all fronts during the Yom Kippur holiday. This measure is to counter potential threats. The news was reported by Ashkan Safaei, a journalist from Iran International.

Kim Jong-pyo, the South Korean ambassador to Iran, performed the song "Sultan of Hearts" on the 64th anniversary of diplomatic relations. The performance was with the Mitra Orchestra. The South Korean embassy described this as a musical gift to show respect and affection for Iran and its culture.
A father of a child told Iran International in a video that he paid over 1.2 million tomans for fever and pain-reducing medications and iron deficiency prevention drugs for his child.

Masoumeh Taherkhani stated that land routes cannot replace maritime trade due to logistical limitations. Turkey is currently extracting monopoly tolls from Iran. Financial routes are also being blocked, which could impose a heavy inflation wave on Iranian consumers by the end of the year.

Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, stated in an online speech that sustainable security in the Middle East must belong to the region itself and is achieved through dialogue and cooperation. He described the military aggression by the US and Israel as illegal and unjust. He also said the war against Iran is part of a broader pattern of unpunished aggressions.
The police commander of Astaneh Ashrafiyeh announced the arrest of a citizen. The reason for the arrest was sending videos to foreign media. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Tuition fees at some private schools in Tehran have reached several hundred million tomans. Parents say that additional costs such as transportation, food, and extracurricular activities have put heavy financial pressure on families. This issue was discussed in an interview with psychoanalyst Saba Alaleh.

A citizen sent a voice message to Iran International mentioning the lack of security in schools. He said he would not send his child to school for a while. He also urged other citizens to take similar action.

Somayeh Golpour stated that less than 5% of workers in the country are members of labor organizations, and 97% have no representatives in higher labor organizations. She criticized the limited meetings of the Supreme Labor Council and the one-year extension of organizations without elections. She considered these factors as weakening the workers' ability to demand rights.

Employees of Refah store reported months of delayed salary payments and unpaid insurance premiums. Their insurance premiums have not been paid for nearly a year. They have called on the Ministry of Cooperatives, Labor, and Social Welfare and the Social Security Organization to address their situation.

Mehdi Kazemi-Qomi stated that 50 to 60 percent of the residential area in Tehran's District 11 is located in worn-out urban fabric. About 371 hectares of this district's land are in the worn-out area, ranking second after District 12. Due to its historical background and high population density, this district is prioritized in urban renewal programs.
Iranians in Australia gathered in Perth on Saturday, 28 Shahrivar. They commemorated Mahsa Amini and chanted the slogan "Regime change" in Iran. These images were published by Iran International.
The opening ceremony of the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games ended an hour ago. The Iranian delegation left their place after the parade and during the ceremony. This caused disorder in the event.
Iranians in Hobart, Australia, held a gathering to commemorate Mahsa Amini. They called for global action regarding Iran. This video was published by Iran International.

Hossein Allahkaram stated that during the funeral ceremonies of Ali Khamenei, the IRGC targeted three large ships belonging to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE. The Supreme National Security Council called these attacks unauthorized, and the naval commander was reprimanded. This incident indicates a breach of the agreement between the Islamic Republic and the United States.

The mother of Hamid Zareh explained how her son was killed by Islamic Republic agents in January 2026. She said she will seek justice for her son's blood. She emphasized that she will stand firm until the end.

The director general of education in Gilan province announced that 1544 students in the province have dropped out of school. This figure highlights existing challenges in the education sector in Gilan. Efforts to address this issue are ongoing.

Anshan Khosravi, an organizer of the Stockholm gathering on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death, stated that they continue the path of Mahsa and other martyrs for freedom. They believe that together they will reach a free Iran. These remarks were made to an Iran International reporter.

Protesting customers of Kerman Motor gathered at the company's headquarters in Tehran. They claim the company does not deliver registered vehicles and refuses to refund payments. The protest took place in the Jannat Abad neighborhood.

The Central Committee of the Ministry of Science confirmed the expulsion of three students from Sharif University of Technology and Beheshti University related to the protests of Esfand 1404. One student was also banned from studying for five years in addition to expulsion. For the other two students, the expulsion can be changed to a three-semester suspension if they express remorse.

Ziba Aflatoun, captain of Iran's women's national basketball team in the 1974 Asian Games, spoke about the support of Empress Farah Pahlavi for women's sports, saying they encouraged and supported basketball to progress. This interview was conducted in a special program for the 2026 Asian Games.

Donald Trump, the US president, signed a bill authorizing new sanctions against Russia over the war in Ukraine. The law also extends sanctions related to Iran. This action followed congressional approval earlier this week.

Tehran's prosecutor has filed charges against the organizers of a 10-kilometer running race in Velayat Park. The race was held with men and women participating and allegedly did not comply with legal and religious regulations. The organizers claim the event was authorized by the Ministry of Interior and the Tehran Athletics Board.

Abbas Araghchi criticized military interventions in the Middle East as a cause of instability and ongoing tensions in a video message to the 2026 Global Dialogue Forum participants. He emphasized that war has become a common tool in international relations rather than a last resort. Araghchi stated that pressure and bullying never lead to peace.
A citizen stated in a video that due to rising prices, they must work 9 hours a day to buy a few groceries. This highlights the economic pressure on people. The video was sent to Iran International.

A spontaneous campaign among Iranian families has formed to boycott in-person classes. The presence of security forces and concerns about the outbreak of war are cited as reasons for the boycott. This issue was discussed in an interview with Mohsen Mohimeni.

Iran International reported the transfer of Iran's oil sales to four new trusts linked to Mohammad Javad Bavand. This issue has also been reflected in domestic media. More details are provided in an interview with Mahtab Gholizadeh.

Ali Zeinivand, spokesperson of the Ministry of Interior, stated that the 10-kilometer marathon in Tehran should not have been held simultaneously with the Janfada exercise. The Tehran prosecutor's office has filed charges against the organizers for not adhering to legal and religious regulations. The event took place on September 17, 2026, and women participated without mandatory hijab.

The expulsion and suspension rulings for Alireza Jafarzadeh from Shahid Beheshti University and Fariborz Kohanzad and Parnian Khodabakhshi from Sharif University of Technology were confirmed by the Central Disciplinary Committee of the Ministry of Science. These rulings involve three students in Tehran. The Ministry of Science has approved these rulings.

The Iranian men's handball team lost their first match on September 18th against Kuwait with a score of 26 to 24. This team was the only Iranian representative on that day. More details are provided in an interview with Alireza Modiri.

Amnesty International has published a detailed report of over 1100 pages on the crimes of the Islamic Republic in suppressing the Mahsa uprising protests. The report accuses Iranian officials of crimes against humanity. The short documentary "Iran Rising" reviews this report and the events of 2022 in Iran.

Schools reopened on September 19, but there are concerns about students' safety and rising costs. Families are avoiding sending their children to school due to war conditions and military training. Economic difficulties have also made school supplies and meals very expensive.

Iranians worldwide held protests on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. Matin Khaledi, an organizer in Florence, stated the aim was to honor the deceased and support prisoners awaiting execution. They also emphasized the leadership of Prince Reza Pahlavi and the national revolution.

Luqman Pourmand, a citizen from Dizaj Margur in Urmia, has been detained for over six months. His family and lawyer have no information about his whereabouts or condition. During this time, he has been denied access to his lawyer and family visits.

The US case against Halkbank was closed on June 17. Two months and 18 days later, the US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank in Turkey. Mohammad Mashinchian reviews the history of sanctions from Pamukbank to Golden Global.

Mike Johnson, Speaker of the US House of Representatives, said the conflict with the Islamic Republic is not an ongoing war and is in its final stage. He emphasized the importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz open for commercial shipping and noted that at least 25 countries can participate in this effort. Johnson called the 'Epic Wrath' operation successful and opposed limiting the US president's military powers.
